summary: The County Attorney is reported to have advised that a blanket moratorium likely lacks legal standing in Virginia because localities must consider each rezoning or special exception application on its individual merits.

source.citation: Regional reporting, July through September 2026; advocacy accounts

notes: Bears on comparison across states. A land use moratorium adopted by resolution in an Oregon city may not be available in the same form in Virginia. A neighboring Virginia city is reported to distinguish a pause pending ordinance revision from a moratorium, described there as a total wipeout of one specific use.
confidence_note: No written opinion has been read. The advice is reported rather than published. Virginia statutory authority for local moratoria is NOT_CHECKED and no Virginia Code section is cited here.
